subject: Another(!) update of the transition guide

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Another(!) update of the transition guide
parts:
Greetings all:

Another iteration of the transition guide is submitted for your
approval. The base font has been changed to Charter (in the mathdesign
package), which is part of the MiKTeX-2.9 distribution and AFAIK the
TeXLive distribution, but it's not too difficult to modify if
necessary. The TOC is now two columns in a Helvetica font, using the
multitoc package in LaTeX. I also changed to double quotes in the code
because straight quotes are easier to read in code than curly ones.

The major set of changes, due to a request by Brian Danielak, occurs
in the section on guides. Tables of the arguments common to both
functions, as well as those specific to one of them, are included, as
well as an expanded discussion about how to call the guide functions.
Let me know if that works (or not).

The included pdf is set up for color highlighting with color graphics,
some of which may not show up particularly well on a B/W printer. In
the previous update, I pushed separate versions for color and B/W
printing to GitHub; in this update, there will only be one .Rnw file
which uses conditional evaluation to toggle color or black and white
versions of the document, which should be up shortly. If you want a
B/W friendly version, make the following changes in the .Rnw file:

(i) in the code chunk immediately after \begin{document}, set
bw_version <- TRUE
(ii) in the \SweaveOpts{} call immediately before the first \section{}
statement, replace highlight=TRUE with highlight=FALSE.

Save the changes and then run it in R (with packages ggplot2-0.9.0,
scales and knitr loaded) as follows:
knit('ggplot2-0.9.0.Rnw')

This produces a .tex file of the same root name in the current R
directory that can be processed with pdflatex in your favorite way.
Yihui has a way to automate this with the devel version of knitr, but
I haven't got it to work just yet. Hopefully by the final version....

Thanks to Yihui Xie, Baptiste Auguie and Brian Danielak for valuable
comments and insights that led to changes in this version.

Dennis

Dennis,

That table is perfect! That's exactly what I was envisioning. Thanks for taking the time to put it together. I really like how it centralizes the information about the user-facing changes to guides(). 

I really appreciate your hard work!

- Brian
